ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that AD is the median of side BC in $\triangle ABC$. A line is drawn through the centroid G, $GE\parallel AC$, intersecting BC at point E. If $DE=2$, what is the length of BC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $G$ is the centroid,\\
hence $DG : DA = 1 : 3$,\\
since $GE \parallel AC$,\\
hence $DE : DC = DG : DA = 1 : 3$,\\
since $DE = 2$,\\
hence $CD = 6$,\\
therefore $BC = 2CD = \boxed{12}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, with A above, and B, D, E, C on the same straight line on the base, in the order B-D-E-C. Segment AD connects from vertex A to point D on the base; point G is located on AD; from G, segment GE is drawn toward the base, intersecting the base at E, and the problem gives that GE ∥ AC. Reasoning: AD is the median on side BC, so D is the midpoint of BC, DC = BC/2. G is the centroid of the triangle, and the centroid on a median satisfies AG:GD = 2:1, therefore DG:DA = 1:3. In triangle DAC, G is on DA, E is on DC, and GE ∥ AC, so triangle DGE and triangle DAC are similar, giving DE/DC = DG/DA = 1/3. Given DE = 2, therefore DC = 6. Also because D is the midpoint of BC, BC = 2DC = 12.
